FROM orders

  AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'

truths.CP4:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per known customer with at least one order in 2025
  SELECT o.customer_id,
         DATE '2025-12-31' - MAX(CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE)) AS recency_days,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders,
         SUM(ol.quantity * ol.unit_price_eur - ol.line_discount_eur) AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN order_lines AS ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
),
scores AS (
  -- one row per customer, with its R, F and M scores
  SELECT customer_id, revenue_eur,
         NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days DESC, customer_id) AS r_score,
         CASE WHEN n_orders >= 6 THEN 5
              WHEN n_orders >= 4 THEN 4
              WHEN n_orders = 3 THEN 3
              WHEN n_orders = 2 THEN 2
              ELSE 1 END AS f_score,
         NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY revenue_eur, customer_id) AS m_score
  FROM customer_orders
),
segments AS (
  -- one row per customer, with its segment
  SELECT revenue_eur,
         CASE WHEN r_score >= 4 AND f_score >= 4 AND m_score >= 4 THEN 'champions'
              WHEN f_score >= 4 THEN 'loyal'
              WHEN r_score <= 2 AND f_score >= 3 THEN 'at_risk'
              WHEN r_score >= 4 AND f_score = 1 THEN 'new'
              WHEN r_score <= 2 THEN 'hibernating'
              ELSE 'others' END AS segment
  FROM scores
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN segment = 'at_risk' THEN revenue_eur ELSE 0 END) / SUM(revenue_eur), 1)
FROM segments

CP1.explanation: RFM scores the customers active in the chosen window, so every known customer with a 2025 order counts, one-order customers included as F 1; a guest order has no customer_id to link it to a person, and 2024-only buyers fall outside the window.

CP5.explanation: RFM describes past orders, so it finds who slipped away but not what a voucher would do, which a random hold-out group measures; a low R score does not show that a voucher works, and customers who lapsed have not all left for good.
